edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 2

source_text: Sponsa ergo orans dicit: Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui. Non unum osculum, sed oscula desiderat. Oscula Verbi sunt illuminationes et doctrinae quibus anima tangitur. Quamdiu per prophetas et legem oscula mittebantur, nondum ipsius oris sponsi osculum datum erat. Nunc autem sponsa perfectior ipsum Verbum desiderat sibi praesens adesse et ore ad os loqui, sicut Moysi dictum est.
pass_a_gloss: Bride therefore praying says: Let-him-kiss me from kisses of-mouth of-him. Not one kiss, but kisses she-desires. Kisses of-Word are illuminations and teachings by-which soul is-touched. As-long-as through prophets and law kisses were-being-sent, not-yet of-itself mouth of-bridegroom kiss given was...
pass_b_english: The Bride therefore prays and says: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. She desires not one kiss but kisses. The kisses of the Word are illuminations and teachings by which the soul is touched. So long as kisses were sent through the prophets and the law, the kiss of the Bridegroom’s own mouth had not yet been given. But now the more perfect Bride desires that the Word himself be present to her and speak mouth to mouth, as was said to Moses.
